purpose: The five measurement events this site records, defined precisely enough that whoever wires them cannot guess, plus the honest current state of each. Defining an event is not collecting it: the counter and the self-hosted endpoint are shipped (2026-11-17), but nothing counts until the owner deploys the endpoint on a host they control and points data/config.json at it. Every count in this file is empty on purpose.
why_nothing_is_sending: The counter and the endpoint code are shipped: assets/app.js carries EV-01 to EV-04 and platform/analytics/server.py is a deployable, tested receiver. But this repository is static files on GitHub Pages - there is no always-on host inside it, so the endpoint has nowhere to run until the owner deploys it (one command; see platform/analytics/README.md).

Until data/config.json carries the endpoint URL, the shipped counter is inert by construction: the script exits before sending anything and stores nothing in the visitor's browser. Nothing counts today, and the footer says exactly that.

The footer states, truthfully today, that the site sets no cookies and that the counter records nothing until an endpoint is configured. Program Policies section 3(e) requires an accurate statement of cookie and third-party technology use, so the build guard check_analytics_disclosure() fails the build the moment the footer statement and the configured state disagree - the sentence cannot be left behind when the beacon turns on.
A click counter that reported a number without a real endpoint behind it would be an invented number on a page that promises every value is sourced. Nothing here reports a count it did not measure.
Amazon's own conversion reporting lives in Associates Central and is not available to a third-party static site, so reported orders must come from the owner's first-party report, not from this site.

shipped.detail: EV-01 page_view (article, product, comparison and guide pages), EV-02 outbound_product_click (real clicks on tagged /dp/ links), EV-03 guide_completed (the final section heading enters the viewport), EV-04 comparison_table_viewed (the comparison matrix enters the viewport). Cookie-free, identifier-free; skips automation and prefetch.

Accepts EV-01 to EV-04 only, rejects EV-05 and any unknown field with HTTP 400, never reads the client address, User-Agent or Referer, drops prefetch beacons unrecorded, stores JSONL locally and serves per-day aggregates at GET /report.

shipped.component: footer cookie / third-party statement (Program Policies section 3(e))
shipped.state: shipped, generated from data/config.json in the same build as the counter
shipped.detail: The build guard check_analytics_disclosure() fails the build if the footer wording and the configured counter state disagree, in either direction.
A row may only be added from an authorised first-party report. No conversion score and no revenue forecast is presented anywhere in this repository.

privacy_rules: No cookies are set by the counter. If a cookie is ever added, the footer statement and the section 3(e) disclosure change in the same commit (enforced by check_analytics_disclosure()).
No persistent identifier per reader and no cross-site profile. Program Policies section 2(b) separately forbids associating a sub-tag with a specific end user.

The counter records the event, the page slug and the product ASIN - never an IP address, user agent string or referrer. The endpoint structurally cannot store them: it never reads those headers, and its schema rejects unknown fields (proven by platform/analytics/test_server.py).

Program Policies section 3(s) forbids artificially generating clicks; the counter is attached to a real click only, skips navigator.webdriver sessions, and the endpoint drops prefetch/prerender beacons unrecorded.

events.name: page_view
events.fires_when: A human opens any article, product, comparison or guide page.
records: whether the arrival carried a utm_source/campaign parameter
events.note: Slug and date only. A per-reader identifier would turn this into behavioural tracking and break the no-cookie statement.

events.name: outbound_click
events.fires_when: A reader clicks any link whose href points at www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>.
records: page slug the click came from
the Associates tag present on the link
events.note: This is the earliest point at which this site can observe intent without Amazon's data. It counts interest, not revenue, and must never be labelled a conversion.

events.name: article_engagement
events.fires_when: A reader scrolls a sourced guide to its final section, measured at the last heading, not the footer.
events.note: A single completion flag is enough to answer 'did anyone read this'. A depth histogram costs a cookie-free session id and buys nothing the editorial calendar uses.

events.name: comparison_interaction
events.fires_when: The comparison table becomes visible in the viewport on compare.html or a product page.
events.note: Exists to test one editorial hypothesis: whether the comparison table is the page's centre of gravity. One boolean per view is the whole signal.

events.name: affiliate_report_import
events.fires_when: Never automatically. Entered by hand from an Amazon Associates Central order report for a dated period.
explicitly_not_recorded: a conversion rate computed from mismatched windows
events.note: The only revenue-bearing event, and it is first-party: it comes from the owner's authorised report, never from this site. The receiver rejects it with HTTP 400 by design. A score or forecast is deliberately absent.

campaign_ledger.note: Started empty on purpose, per the brief's 'empty but well-defined campaign ledger'. A row may only be added from an authorised first-party report. No conversion score and no revenue forecast is presented anywhere in this repository.
campaign_ledger.why_empty: No first-party analytics exist yet, the endpoint is not deployed, and no Associates report has been read into this repository. An empty ledger is a true statement; a filled one would not be.

prerequisites.owner_action: Deploy platform/analytics/server.py on a host you control behind TLS (one command; see platform/analytics/README.md) and note its public https://…/e URL.
prerequisites.why: A static GitHub Pages repo cannot receive a beacon. The receiver is shipped and tested; it only needs a host.

prerequisites.owner_action: Set analytics_endpoint in data/config.json to that URL and rebuild (or merge the change this repo prepares).
prerequisites.why: The counter reads the endpoint from the page. The footer's §3(e) sentence updates automatically in the same build; the guard check_analytics_disclosure() enforces it.

prerequisites.owner_action: Report the Associates tracking ID in use and confirm the account is approved; read one dated order report and enter it as the ledger's first row (EV-05).
prerequisites.why: Reported orders are first-party data from Associates Central. Nothing on this site may model them.

prerequisites.owner_action: Verify the site in Google Search Console and share the Search Queries report for the dated period.
prerequisites.blocks: Choosing the next topic from measured queries
prerequisites.why: The brief says the next topic must be chosen from measured queries instead of instinct; that needs the query report, which only the verified property owner can read.

merged_with_analytics_plan: 2026-11-17 (arena/c9e97e02 rebase): data/analytics-plan.json (session 5b17c077 lineage) defines the same five events under project names (page_view, outbound_click, article_engagement, comparison_interaction, affiliate_report_import). The shipped counter now speaks the plan's names; the EV ids below are this file's stable ids. Enable exactly one collection path — the counter via data/config.json analytics_endpoint, or the plan's same-origin collector via its deployment gates — never both.
measurement_status: Counter and self-hosted receiver are code-complete with tests (2026-11-17); no host is deployed, analytics_endpoint is empty, so nothing is recorded. No count is published anywhere. The page is generated from these definitions; the footer §3(e) sentence is generated from the same config value and a build guard (check_analytics_disclosure) keeps the two in step.
